slides.title: Setosa petals form a distinct cluster
slides.caption: One dot per plant. Equal lengths stack vertically within each species.
slides.notes: Follow the horizontal axis first. There are 50 plants in each row. The amount of stacking shows how frequently each recorded length occurs.

slides.title: Virginica petals average {{virginica}}
slides.notes: Each bar is the arithmetic mean for 50 observations. The title, labels and difference use the same three-decimal source table. Values on screen are rounded to two decimals.

slides.title: Versicolor and virginica overlap in petal length
slides.notes: Versicolor ranges from 3.0 to 5.1 cm and virginica from 4.5 to 6.9 cm. The intervals overlap even though the means differ.
slides.caption: Compare the minimum for virginica with the maximum for versicolor.

slides.title: A single petal length can fit either species
slides.label: Shared interval of the observed ranges
slides.heading: Where the ranges meet
slides.text: A measurement in this interval is compatible with both observed ranges. The next comparison should include petal width.
slides.notes: Range overlap does not imply identical frequencies or a classification error rate. The interval is computed from the virginica minimum and the versicolor maximum.
